source_row.item_data_json: {"options":{"A":"Hypernatremia, commonly reflecting a relative free-water deficit and causing neurologic symptoms","B":"Hyponatremia, commonly reflecting excess free water and producing the measured sodium value","C":"Hyperkalemia, because potassium excess directly explains an elevated measured sodium level","D":"A normal sodium concentration, because symptoms are unrelated to the laboratory measurement"}}
source_row.rationale: A sodium concentration above the usual reference range is hypernatremia. It commonly reflects water deficit relative to sodium and may produce thirst and neurologic manifestations such as restlessness or confusion.
source_row.source_detail: High blood sodium (hypernatremia) and associated symptoms/causes; U.S. National Library of Medicine; accessed 2026-08-14.
source_row.stem: A client has a serum sodium of 152 mEq/L with intense thirst, restlessness, and confusion. Which interpretation is most accurate?
